findings.title: Team admin permission requires user to be both admin AND owner
findings.body: The permission check `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` requires the caller to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner. Since `isTeamAdmin` typically already returns true for owners, the AND collapses the check to "owner only" — team admins lose the ability to add guests. The operator should be `||` (or the `isTeamAdmin` call should be dropped, as it already covers owners). With the current code, only team owners can use the new feature even though the UI claims any admin/owner can.

findings.title: Team bookings crash with Prisma RecordNotFound
findings.body: For team/round-robin bookings, `booking.userId` is often null. The handler does `where: { id: booking.userId || 0 }` when looking up the organizer, so it issues `findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: 0 } })`, which throws an unwrapped `Prisma.RecordNotFound` error and returns a 500 to the client instead of a meaningful error. The lookup needs to handle `booking.userId == null` explicitly (e.g. resolve the organizer from `eventType.team` or return a clean `NOT_FOUND`/`BAD_REQUEST`).

findings.title: Deduplication is case-sensitive, allowing near-duplicate attendees
findings.body: Both the existing-attendee check (`guest === attendee.email`) and the email format assumed by the rest of the app treat emails as case-sensitive, but emails are case-insensitive by RFC. A caller can submit `Alice@Example.com` while an existing attendee is `alice@example.com` and the new one will be added as a separate row, creating duplicate attendees in `Booking.attendees` and duplicate calendar invites. All comparisons should lowercase both sides before comparing, and the schema should normalize input.

findings.title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive
findings.body: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is lowercased on parse, but the input `guest` is not lowercased before `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Submitting `BLOCKED@example.com` against a blacklist entry `blocked@example.com` will bypass the block. The guest value must be lowercased before being checked against the blacklist.

findings.title: Server-side schema does not enforce uniqueness, allowing duplicate rows
findings.body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates email format; uniqueness is only enforced in the client `AddGuestsDialog`. A malicious or buggy client can POST `["a@x.com", "a@x.com"]` and the handler will create two `Attendee` rows for the same address. The server schema should `.refine` for uniqueness (ideally after lowercasing) and the handler's `uniqueGuests` filter should also be the source of truth for the DB write — currently `prisma.booking.update(... createMany: data: guestsFullDetails)` uses `uniqueGuests`, but the email pass later (`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`) uses the raw `guests` input, which can still mis-trigger the duplicate `AttendeeScheduledEmail` branch in `email-manager.ts`.

findings.title: No transactional boundary between DB write and calendar/email side effects
findings.body: `prisma.booking.update` runs first, then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, then `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. None of this is in a transaction. If the calendar call or email send throws, the DB is left with attendees added but the connected calendar/videocall still missing them, and the user sees a 500 even though the mutation was half-applied. The whole flow should be wrapped (DB update + calendar update + email send) so a failure leaves no partial state, or the email/calendar steps should run before the DB write with a compensating delete on failure.

findings.title: Email send failure is silently swallowed
findings.body: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` call is wrapped in `try { ... } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`. The DB has already been mutated and the calendar has already been updated, so the API returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` and the UI shows the success toast even when no emails went out. Either surface the error (so the UI can retry/notify) or skip the DB write until emails have been queued.

findings.title: Cancelled/rejected/past bookings can have guests added
findings.body: After loading the booking, the handler never checks `booking.status`. A caller can add guests to a CANCELLED, REJECTED, or already-past booking, which will create new attendees, push them to the connected calendar, and send "guests added" emails about an event that is no longer happening. The handler must reject when the booking is not in an `ACCEPTED` (or `PENDING`) state, and ideally also when `booking.endTime < now()`.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails sends AttendeeScheduledEmail to new guests using raw input emails
findings.body: The handler passes the raw `guests` input (which may contain case variants or duplicates) as `newGuests`, and `sendAddGuestsEmails` does `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide between `AttendeeScheduledEmail` and `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Because the match is case-sensitive and the input was not deduplicated/normalized, the wrong email template is sent in the obvious cases (e.g. `Alice@x.com` vs `alice@x.com`) and a duplicate email is sent if the same address was submitted twice with different casing. The list of "new" guests should be built from the normalized `uniqueGuests` and lowercased before comparison.

findings.title: Dialog sends empty email rows through validation and fails with a misleading message
findings.body: `MultiEmail` initializes `value` with `[""]` and the "Add Another" button pushes another `""`. The dialog validates the raw `multiEmailValue` array, so leaving any field blank (e.g. `["a@x.com", "", "b@x.com"]`) or submitting immediately on open fails `z.array(z.string().email())` and shows "Emails must be unique and valid", which does not describe the actual problem (blank fields). The handler should `.transform`/filter out empty strings (and lowercase + trim) before parsing, and surface a more specific message — otherwise users will repeatedly hit this confusing error.

findings.title: Error toast displays raw TRPC code instead of a useful translation key
findings.body: On error the toast uses `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. For zod-input failures `err.message` is a generic zod string (e.g. the literal string `"BAD_REQUEST"` is not a translation key), so users see `BAD_REQUEST: BAD_REQUEST` or a missing-translation key. The handler should throw `TRPCError`s with translation-key messages (like the existing `emails_must_be_unique_valid`/`you_do_not_have_permission`), and the client should prefer `t(err.message)` only when the key exists, falling back to `unable_to_add_guests` otherwise.

findings.title: userPrimaryEmail is always undefined, silently falling back to organizer.email
findings.body: The Prisma `booking` query does not select `userPrimaryEmail`, so `booking?.userPrimaryEmail ?? organizer.email` always resolves to `organizer.email`. This is unlikely to be a security issue (the booking's organizer email is also pulled from the same user record), but the misleading fallback hides the intent. If the original design is to honor the organizer's primary email for calendar invites, the field needs to be added to the `select`/`include`; otherwise the dead branch should be removed.

findings.title: No upper bound on guests array length
findings.body: The schema accepts an unbounded array of emails and the handler will happily create that many attendees, update the calendar, and fan out N emails. A malicious caller can submit thousands of addresses to cause resource exhaustion and email bombing. Add `z.array(...).min(1).max(N)` (with N chosen to match the event type's `seatsPerTimeSlot` / max attendees setting) and consider reusing `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` plus rate limiting.

findings.title: {...props} spread after named props allows caller to silently override intended fields
findings.body: `{...props}` is spread after `title`, `headerType`, `subject`, and `callToAction`, so if any caller (including `organizer-add-guests-email.ts` if extended) ever passes one of those keys, the intended value is silently overridden. Move `{...props}` before the named props, or destructure them out of `props` before spreading. The same pattern exists in `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail.tsx`.

findings.title: AddGuestsDialog is always mounted for every booking row
findings.body: The `<AddGuestsDialog>` is rendered unconditionally for every `BookingListItem` (and the BookingListItem table can render hundreds of rows). The dialog content is always in the DOM, registering tRPC mutation hooks for every row. The dialog should only be mounted when `isOpenAddGuestsDialog` is true (the same pattern other dialogs in this file already use), to avoid hundreds of stale mutation handles and extra DOM nodes on the bookings list page.
